Aghoraśivācārya
a Śaiva writer; disciple of Vidyākaṇṭha, the disciple of Rāmakaṇṭha, [Page058-b] who was the son of Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha an. disciple of Utpala (Hz. II. Extr. p. 109); wrote the Mṛgendravṛttidīpikā a. the instance of this Guru; Sarvātmaśiva is usually mentioned a. his chief Guru; was born in the Col. country in the Kauṇḍinyagotra; had the title ‘Lakṣadvayādhyāpaka’, teacher of Mīmāṁsā which is called ‘Lakṣadvaya (?)’; see p. 7. English Intro. to the Bṛhatī, Madras Uni. Skt. Ser. III. ii; mentioned sometimes a. Ghoraśiva an. Parameśvara (MT. 2104) also; known a. Jñānaśiva too (MD. 5436) (?); mentions in the Kriyākramadyotikā that he wrote it in Śaka 1080, A. D. 1157. See p. 4, Skt. Intro. to the Chidambaram Grantha edn. of 1927 of the Kriyākramadyotikā in part an. p. 6, Intro. Devakottah Śivāgama Siddhānta Paripālana Saṅgha edn. of the Tattvaprakāśa.
According to Trilocanaśivācārya (Prāyaścittasamuccaya, Hz. 954), Aghoraśivācārya was one of the spiritual heads of the seat called Āmardakamaṭha (Hz. II. Extr. p. 80). Sage Āmardaka was one of the disciples of Durvāsas an. the founder of dualistic Śaiva.
A traditional version of his story is found in a work called Cidambarasāra. See Tamil Preface to the abovementioned edn. of the Kriyākramadyotikā. This preface an. the Skt. Intro. referred to previously give a list of Āghoraśivācārya's works. Works marked with a. asterisk below are refered to by the a. himself in his Ratnatrayollekhinī (See p. 108 of the Devakottah Śivāgama Siddhānta Paripālana [Page059-a. Saṅgha edn.) an.
